'''MYOB''' (meaning ''mind your own business'') is an [[Australia|Australian]] [[multinational corporation]] that provides [[tax]], [[accounting]] and other business services software to small and medium businesses. It is owned by [[Kohlberg Kravis Roberts|KKR]].

==Products==
MYOB has a suite of products spanning the small business accounting software market, the payroll and HRM market, the accountants vertical and mid-market [[enterprise resource planning]] (ERP) market. Whilst there are still some components of the product suites that are [[On-premises software|on-premise]], the majority and all new products are [[cloud-based]]. Most products are sold via the subscription billing model ([[Software as a service|SaaS]]). The first edition of MYOB's small business browser-based software was released in August 2010 and was known as Live Accounts. On 24 October 2012, MYOB released AccountRight Live, an update to its flagship product – a [[Microsoft Windows|Microsoft-Windows]]–only software suite which had online storage of data.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MYOB Launches Australian-First in Cloud Accounting |url=https://www.pr.com/press-release/451406 |access-date=2026-01-10 |website=PR.com |language=en}}</ref>

==History==
MYOB was founded in the early 1980s by a team of developers at Teleware, who developed accounting software. Teleware was purchased by Best Software (now part of [[Sage Group|Sage]]) in 1993. Data-Tech Software was the Australian republisher of the MYOB products and, in 1997 entered into an agreement with [[Best Software]] to buy the company (renamed MYOB Inc.) and bought the intellectual property rights to the software. In 1999, Data-Tech changed its name to MYOB Limited and listed on the [[Australian Securities Exchange]] (ASX). In subsequent corporate development, MYOB Limited merged with Solution 6 Holdings in 2004. Though the company was founded in the United States, it ceased operations outside of Australia and New Zealand in 2008.{{Citation needed|date=June 2024}}

Co-founder Brad Shofer left the company in 2003.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.smh.com.au/small-business/myob-founders-latest-venture-no-dinosaur-20090619-cq2m.html |title= MYOB founder's latest venture no dinosaur |last=Knight |first=Anneli |date=17 December 2007 |website=[[Sydney Morning Herald]]|publisher=Fairfax Media |access-date=4 December 2016}}</ref>

In December 2008, Acclivity announced it acquired MYOB US Inc. and its [[Macintosh]] (and PC) development team from MYOB Limited of Australia. Acclivity now drives global development of MYOB's [[Mac operating systems|Mac OS]] business management products – AccountEdge Basic, AccountEdge Pro and AccountEdge Pro Network Edition.

In January 2009, a [[private equity]] consortium led by [[Archer Capital]] completed a takeover bid for MYOB, returning MYOB to private ownership.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.delisted.com.au/CompanyDisplay.aspx?id=5727 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110706103919/http://www.delisted.com.au/CompanyDisplay.aspx?id=5727 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2011-07-06 |title=MYOB Limited privatised }}</ref>

In August 2011, Archer Capital sold MYOB to [[Bain Capital]] for an undisclosed amount. The acquisition gave Bain Capital a majority stake in MYOB alongside management continued to be shareholders in the company.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://myob.com.au/myob/news-1258090872838?articleId=1257829347489&year=2011 |title=Bain Capital signs definitive agreement with Archer Capital to acquire MYOB Ltd}}</ref>

MYOB Group Limited was readmitted to the official list of the [[Australian Securities Exchange]] in May 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.asx.com.au/asx/research/company.do#!/MYO |title=MYOB Group Limited listed on ASX |access-date=17 May 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304230436/http://www.asx.com.au/asx/research/company.do#!/MYO |archive-date=4 March 2016 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

In November 2017, MYOB proposed to buy [[Reckon (company)|Reckon]]'s accounting group for $180 million.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.afr.com/technology/myob-buys-reckons-accounting-group-for-180-million-20171115-gzme8a|title=Reckon sells 'crown jewel' of the business to MYOB in $180 million deal|date=2017-11-16|work=[[Australian Financial Review]]|access-date=2017-11-17|language=en-US}}</ref> However, failure to obtain regulatory permission caused the deal to fall apart in May 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/business/companies/myob-group-terminates-acquisition-of-reckon-business-20180531-p4zild.html|title=MYOB Group terminates $180m acquisition of Reckon business|date=31 May 2018|website=Sydney Morning Herald}}</ref>

In April 2018, MYOB sold its rental payment system RentPay to [[Rent.com.au]] for $425,000.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.crn.com.au/news/myob-sells-its-rental-business-to-rentcomau-for-425000-489873|title=MYOB sells its rental business to Rent.com.au for $425,000|website=CRN Australia|access-date=2018-05-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://channellife.com.au/story/myob-sells-its-rental-payments-platform-425000/|title=MYOB sells off its rental payments platform for $425,000|access-date=2018-05-31|language=en}}</ref> In May 2018, MYOB partnered with [[Network 10]]'s Shark Tank.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.bandt.com.au/marketing/myob-partners-network-tens-shark-tank|title=MYOB Partners With Network Ten's Shark Tank - B&T|date=2018-05-15|work=B&T|access-date=2018-05-31|language=en-US}}</ref>

MYOB Group Limited was delisted from the ASX in May 2019, after it sold to private equity firm [[Kohlberg Kravis Roberts|KKR]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.afr.com/technology/investors-wave-through-myob-takeover-20190417-p51ew7|title=Investors wave through MYOB takeover|date=2019-04-17|website=[[Australian Financial Review]]|language=en|access-date=2019-08-13}}</ref>

===BankLink===
'''BankLink''' was an [[accounting]] service for [[Value-added tax|GST]] and end of year [[tax]] in Australia and New Zealand.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/business/news/article.cfm?c_id=3&objectid=10815198 |title=BankLink saves businesses time and effort – Business – NZ Herald News |work=The New Zealand Herald |date=2012-06-25 |access-date=2012-09-10}}</ref> BankLink started its business in 1986,<ref>{{cite news |last1=White |first1=Rachel |title=MYOB acquires NZ software rival BankLink |url=https://www.accountingweb.co.uk/tech/accounting-software/myob-acquires-nz-software-rival-banklink |access-date=10 December 2024 |publisher=AccountingWEB |date=17 May 2013}}</ref> and was acquired by MYOB in June 2013.

It was a privately owned business based in Auckland, New Zealand. BankLink launched in the United Kingdom in 2011. In 2012 BankLink partnered with MYOB so that BankLink provided data to be used in MYOB's accounting products.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/BU1206/S00712/myob-and-banklink-announce-strategic-partnership.htm |title=MYOB And Banklink Announce Strategic Partnership | Scoop News |publisher=Scoop.co.nz |date=2012-06-21 |access-date=2012-09-10}}</ref>
